answer: Shared-secret terrace binding. Each agent receives a unique secret at registration and must publish a distinct derived key per action epoch. The registry enforces a collision rule: two identities deriving from the same root secret trigger automatic flagging and freeze. An attacker cloning one agent into many pays full registration cost per duplicate plus forfeiture of the original's harbor credits on detection. Honest agents pay only the one-time ivory issuance fee, keeping duplication economically self-defeating.
